question: Should OpenClaw add an operator-owned `agents.defaults` / per-agent prompt-rules config surface, and what write boundary should protect it?
rationale: This adds a public model-facing config/default surface that can alter safety instructions and session behavior across channels, cron, subagents, and Codex-backed runtimes; source review can prove the gap but not choose the permanent product and security contract.

options.title: Approve narrow operator-owned overlay
options.body: Add an append-only prompt/rules overlay resolved at session creation, inherited from defaults to per-agent config, and keep it out of agent-facing config mutation unless explicitly allowed.

options.title: Defer to broader prompt customization
options.body: Keep this issue open but fold the design into the broader system-prompt customization discussion before adding any new config key.

options.title: Reject core config surface
options.body: Keep workspace files, channel prompts, plugins, and external tooling as the supported rule-management mechanisms, closing this and duplicates as not planned.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow operator-owned overlay
recommendation.body: Add an append-only prompt/rules overlay resolved at session creation, inherited from defaults to per-agent config, and keep it out of agent-facing config mutation unless explicitly allowed.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest prompt/config history trail for deciding whether this becomes a core prompt contract or stays out of core.
